method: Agent-enumerated from domain knowledge cross-checked against events/*.yaml (146 ids) and candidate_triggers/*.yaml. Each candidate verified via WebSearch against contemporaneous Reuters / AP / Guardian / Bloomberg / Al Jazeera / CNN / TechCrunch reporting, primary DOJ / FinCEN / Treasury press releases, and the WikiLeaks Banking-Blockade archive. No automated scraper used.
cross_check_method: Each candidate slug cross-checked against the 146 admitted event ids and the candidate_triggers/ promoted_event_id values. ZERO 2008-2012 events presently in corpus. The closest existing ids by topic are: mtgox-dhs-dwolla-wells-fargo-seizure-2013 / mtgox-bankruptcy-tokyo-2014 (Mt. Gox cascade, but post-tier), btc-e-doj-2017 (Vinnik, post-tier), shrem-faiella-bitcoin-exchange-2014 (BitInstant operator, post-tier), silk-road-doj-seizure-2013 (post-tier). No collisions.
exclusion_notes: DigiCash / E-Cash 1999-era is outside tier (predates 2008 lower bound by ~9 years). Liberty Reserve is the conceptual successor and is captured here.

Pecunix winding-down 2008-2011 has no clean primary regulator action or contemporaneous news pin (the 2008 bullion transfer was a private corporate move). Marked P2 / deferred for lack of an enforceable trigger date.
GoldMoney KYC tightening 2008-2010 has no contemporaneous primary regulator filing; the trajectory is documented only via corporate blog and customer reviews. Marked P2 / deferred.

Liberty Reserve §311 FinCEN designation 2013-05-28 + DOJ takedown is OUTSIDE this tier (post-2012). It is the documented endpoint of the 2009-2012 Liberty Reserve trajectory but should be carried in a historical_baseline_2013_2016 candidate or admitted to that tier instead. NOT enumerated here.

Silk Road pre-arrest 2011-2012 LE attention is documented only via post-hoc DOJ filings (Ulbricht complaint Sep 2013); no contemporaneous 2011-2012 enforcement publication exists. Pre-arrest LE attention is not enumerated as a separate candidate.

Iran-sanctions / DPRK-sanctions 2008-2011 financial-system actions (correspondent severance, OFAC SDN updates) are broad sanctions-policy actions outside this dataset's chain-censorship scope, except for the 2012 SWIFT disconnection (P2: useful as a non-crypto comparator showing the parallel mechanism, but cascade observability for chain layers is weak).
Operation Payback DDoS retaliation against Visa/MasterCard 2010-12-08 is a third-party cyber response to the blockade, not a censorship event itself. Documented in context but not enumerated.
stratum_terminology_note: Existing corpus uses S1_ofac_sdn / S3_doj_sec_cftc_fiod / S4_nation_state / S5_corporate. For pre-Bitcoin baseline, corporate financial-intermediary actions (PayPal, Visa, MasterCard, Bank of America, Western Union, PostFinance, Amazon, EveryDNS) map to S5_corporate; DOJ / Secret Service criminal actions (e-Gold, e-Bullion) map to S3_doj_sec_cftc_fiod; FBI intelligence assessments map to S3_doj_sec_cftc_fiod (policy-class); Iceland court rulings on the blockade map to S4_nation_state (judicial sub-stratum). Mt. Gox 2011 hack / Bitcoinica 2012 hack are operator-self-inflicted compromises (S0_operator_action if such stratum exists; otherwise treat as private operator-collapse precedents alongside the 2016 Bitfinex / Cryptsy historical-baseline cases).

candidates.title: PayPal freezes WikiLeaks donations account (Wau-Holland-Stiftung)
candidates.rationale: Foundational event of the WikiLeaks banking-blockade case study. PayPal notice dated 2010-12-03, public effect 2010-12-04, froze the Wau-Holland-Stiftung donations account (which had collected $1.9M for WikiLeaks Oct 2009-Dec 2010) and held remaining balance for 180 days. PayPal VP Osama Bedier (LeWeb Paris 2010-12-08) named the State Department as cited cause. Cleanest single-corporate-intermediary L4/L5 censorship action in the 2008-2012 tier with abundant Reuters/AP/Bloomberg coverage. Paper-impactful precedent: the foundational case in the academic literature on payment-network censorship.

candidates.title: MasterCard suspends WikiLeaks payment processing
candidates.rationale: MasterCard publicly suspended processing of WikiLeaks donations 2010-12-06, citing 'illegal activity' without identifying any specific statutory violation. Triggered Operation Payback DDoS retaliation (2010-12-08, third-party, not enumerated). One of the two card-network legs of the blockade. Cleanest example of corporate card-network access censorship outside any judicial finding. Companion to wikileaks-visa-suspension-2010-12.

candidates.title: Visa Europe suspends WikiLeaks payment processing (Teller/Korta DataCell gateway)
candidates.rationale: Visa Europe via acquirer Teller A/S (Denmark) and Korta hf. (Iceland) terminated the DataCell ehf merchant agreement 2010-12-07 without notice, blocking the credit-card gateway DataCell had set up under a 2010-10-18 services contract to process WikiLeaks donations. The Visa leg of the card-network blockade. This is the trigger that directly led to the DataCell v. Valitor litigation in Iceland 2012-2013 (separate candidate). Cascade: 95% revenue drop for WikiLeaks per Assange's Oct 2011 statement.

candidates.title: Bank of America halts all WikiLeaks-related transactions
candidates.rationale: BoA announced 2010-12-18 that it would 'no longer process any transactions that it believes are intended for [WikiLeaks]', citing 'reasonable belief that WikiLeaks may be engaged in activities that are ... inconsistent with our internal policies for processing payments.' Notable as the only US-domiciled commercial bank action in the blockade; later context for the Anonymous/HBGary/BoA leak-strategy memos 2011 and the 2011-12 Wired Magazine reporting on the BoA-WikiLeaks defense playbook.

candidates.title: Western Union adds WikiLeaks to Interdiction List
candidates.rationale: Western Union added WikiLeaks to its internal 'Interdiction List' on 2010-12-21, refusing to process any remittance involving WikiLeaks or any of its known recipient addresses. Documented in the WikiLeaks Banking-Blockade archive and the Defend-WikiLeaks timeline. Marks the remittance-network leg of the blockade (distinct from card networks and commercial banks). `needs_check`: WU never issued a contemporaneous press statement; the action is documented via internal Interdiction-List leaks and the WikiLeaks archive only. Secondary coverage is uneven; admit only with `evidence_use: contextual_unarchived` tag and capture the Defend-WikiLeaks timeline snapshot.

candidates.title: Swiss PostFinance closes Julian Assange's WikiLeaks Defence-Fund account
candidates.rationale: PostFinance (Swiss Post's banking arm) closed Julian Assange's Swiss bank account 2010-12-06, citing alleged false residency information on the account-opening form. The account was the dedicated 'Julian Assange and other WikiLeaks Staff Defence Fund' channel. Triggered Operation Payback DDoS against postfinance.ch 2010-12-06. Important as the only European-state-postal-banking leg of the blockade. Coverage in Bloomberg / Al Jazeera / CBS is consistent and same-day.

candidates.title: Amazon Web Services evicts WikiLeaks from hosting
candidates.rationale: AWS evicted WikiLeaks from its hosting 2010-12-01 after staff inquiry from Sen. Joe Lieberman's office (HSGAC chair). EFF analysis frames this as the canonical case of 'online speech is only as strong as the weakest intermediary' — directly relevant to the L4-frontend / hosting-infrastructure censorship layer. While AWS hosting eviction is not a payment-network action, it is the L4/infrastructure leg of the same coordinated blockade and is paper-impactful precedent for later events in this dataset (cloudflare-ethereum-gateway-tornado-block-2022-08, infura-metamask-donetsk-luhansk-block-2022-03). Schema fit: layer_observations should include hosting/CDN if such layer exists; otherwise l4_frontend.

candidates.title: EveryDNS terminates wikileaks.org DNS service
candidates.rationale: EveryDNS terminated DNS service for wikileaks.org 2010-12-02 at 22:00 EST after sending a 24-hour notice 2010-12-01, citing DDoS that 'threatened the stability of [the EveryDNS] infrastructure supporting ~500,000 other websites.' Half an hour later, secondary domains (wikileaks.ch) were also disabled. Cleanest L0/L1-infrastructure-layer (DNS-resolver) censorship case in the 2008-2012 tier; arguably the most paper-impactful precedent for the 2022 Cloudflare-Tornado/Infura-Donetsk events in this dataset. `needs_check`: EveryDNS framed the action as a TOS violation by WikiLeaks (creating DDoS targeting), not coordinated with the financial blockade — but the timing and the EFF/Register critique both treat it as the same chilling-effect cascade.

candidates.title: DOJ guilty plea: e-Gold Ltd / Gold & Silver Reserve / Douglas Jackson
candidates.rationale: e-Gold Ltd. and Gold & Silver Reserve Inc. pleaded guilty 2008-07-21 (DC) to conspiracy to launder money and operate an unlicensed money-transmitting business. Co-defendants Douglas Jackson (CEO), Reid Jackson, Barry Downey individually pleaded. Trial date end-point of the indictment unsealed 2007-04-27 (separate predicate, see egold-secret-service-indictment-2007-04). Foundational pre-Bitcoin US digital-currency takedown — the single most-cited 2007-2008 precedent for the FinCEN MSB framework that would later be applied to bitcoin businesses. DOJ press release is stable on justice.gov archive. Paper-impactful: the conceptual predecessor to the Liberty Reserve §311 designation 2013-05-28 and the FinCEN FIN-2013-G001 virtual-currency MSB guidance.

candidates.title: US Secret Service / DOJ indictment of e-Gold Ltd + Douglas Jackson + Reid Jackson + Barry Downey
candidates.rationale: Four-count federal indictment of e-Gold Ltd., Gold & Silver Reserve Inc., and the three principals returned 2007-04-24, unsealed 2007-04-27. Filed in D.D.C. End of a ~2.5-yr USSS Orlando Field Office investigation. Triggered DOJ restraining order + 24 seizure warrants across 58+ e-Gold accounts believed property of money-laundering / unlicensed-MSB violations. Direct precursor to the 2008-07-21 plea. **Outside the strict 2008-2012 lower bound by 8 months** — but the seizure-warrant cascade ran into 2008 and the conduct charged spans 2002-2007. Recommend admit as discovery_only_2008_2012 with admission_tier=precursor or with scope_window note. If the lower bound is rigid 2008-01-01, treat the 2008-07-21 plea as the in-tier anchor and reference this indictment in `related_events`.

candidates.title: DOJ/FBI seizure of e-Bullion (James Fayed) following Pamela Fayed murder
candidates.rationale: US government seized all assets of e-Bullion (Goldfinger Coin and Bullion / James Fayed) August 2008 following the 2008-07-28 murder of co-founder Pamela Fayed. e-Bullion was operating without an MSB license, processing transactions for >1M users with ~50,000 oz gold reserves. Asset returns 2014-2019 totaled ~$23.3M to ~1,000 victims. Companion case to e-Gold for the 2008 digital-gold-currency takedown wave; cleanest precedent for asset-seizure-based deplatforming of a non-blockchain digital-currency exchange. `needs_check`: exact seizure date (warrant date vs. operational shutdown) and the controlling court docket (E-Bullion criminal proceedings were in C.D. Cal.; Fayed murder proceedings were in LA Superior Court). Primary DOJ press releases are 2014/2015/2019 asset-return announcements, not the original 2008 seizure document — pin the original via PACER for body_hash.

candidates.title: Datacell ehf v. Valitor hf. — Reykjavik District Court ruling on Visa-WikiLeaks blockade
candidates.rationale: Reykjavik District Court 2012-07-12 ruled that Valitor hf. (Visa Iceland) closure of the DataCell credit-card gateway on 2010-12-07 was illegal and ordered Valitor to re-open the gateway within 14 days or pay a daily fine of 800,000 ISK (~6,300 USD/day). Supreme Court of Iceland affirmed 2013-04-24 (separate candidate datacell-v-valitor-iceland-supreme-court-2013-04). The first judicial finding anywhere that a card-network blockade of WikiLeaks donations was unlawful. Cleanest non-US-judicial restraint on a card-network payment-censorship action. Paper-impactful: directly relevant to the academic literature on payment-network gatekeeping (Pasquale, Lessig, EFF).

candidates.title: Mt. Gox June 2011 hack and trading suspension
candidates.rationale: 2011-06-19 (Tokyo 2011-06-20 03:00 JST): large sell orders crashed BTC/USD on Mt. Gox from ~$17.50 to $0.01 over several minutes. Mt. Gox took the exchange offline; trading remained suspended through August 2011 while the operator rolled back trades and reset passwords. 25,000 BTC (~$400k) stolen from 478 user accounts. Reported by user @allinvain (Mt. Gox forum) and Bitcoinica/CoinDesk-precursor outlets. First major bitcoin-exchange compromise + operator-imposed access freeze in the dataset. **Operator-self-inflicted compromise**: this is closer to a hack than a censorship action per se, but the multi-week withdrawal freeze is a stratum-S0 / operator-action precedent for the 2014 Mt. Gox collapse and the 2016 Bitfinex hack already in corpus. Admit with caveats.

candidates.title: Bitcoinica shutdown after May 2012 hot-wallet hack (Zhou Tong / Tihan Seale)
candidates.rationale: Bitcoinica (founded 2011 by Zhou Tong, sold to Wendon Group, registered as FSP in NZ April 2012) shut down 2012-05-11 following an 18,547-BTC hot-wallet theft. Earlier loss 43,554 BTC from Linode hack March 2012; later loss 40,000 BTC + $40,000 USD via Mt. Gox account hijack July 2012. Deregistered November 2012. Bitcoinica became a creditor claimant in Mt. Gox 2014 bankruptcy (AUD$42M outstanding). First major margin-trading bitcoin platform collapse; cleanest pre-2014 operator-collapse precedent. Same stratum-S0 / operator-action category as the Mt. Gox 2011 hack candidate.

candidates.title: FBI Directorate of Intelligence — Bitcoin Virtual Currency assessment
candidates.rationale: FBI Directorate of Intelligence (Cyber Intelligence Section + Criminal Intelligence Section) issued 'Bitcoin Virtual Currency: Unique Features Present Distinct Challenges for Deterring Illicit Activity' on 2012-04-24. First FBI intelligence-class document on Bitcoin; estimated Bitcoin economy at $35-44M with ~8.8M BTC in circulation; assessed with medium confidence that cyber-criminals would adopt Bitcoin. Leaked to Wired/CSO May 2012, posted to bitcointalk.org. Policy/intelligence-class trigger (no immediate enforcement action), but the foundational US-federal posture document predating FIN-2013-G001. Schema fit: similar to fincen-virtual-currency-msb-guidance-2013 already enumerated as P0 in historical_baseline_2013_2016 — admit only if intelligence-class triggers with downstream cascade evidence are in scope.

candidates.title: BitInstant launches as bitcoin-cash on-ramp (Shrem + Nelson)
candidates.rationale: BitInstant launched September 2011 (Gareth Nelson + Charlie Shrem); operated 2011-2013, processing ~30% of bitcoin transactions at peak. Receipt for the 2014-01-26 Shrem arrest (already in corpus as shrem-faiella-bitcoin-exchange-2014). The 2011 launch is the operator-formation precedent for the 2014 enforcement; not a censorship event itself. **P2 / deferred**: include as background context for shrem-faiella-bitcoin-exchange-2014, not as an admission-tier candidate. No formal precedent for admitting operator-formation events without an enforcement trigger.

candidates.title: Iceland Supreme Court affirms DataCell v. Valitor (Visa-WikiLeaks blockade)
candidates.rationale: Supreme Court of Iceland 2013-04-24 affirmed the 2012-07-12 Reykjavik District Court ruling that Valitor's Visa-WikiLeaks blockade was unlawful; ordered Valitor to resume processing donations within 2 weeks under daily fine. **OUTSIDE the strict 2008-2012 tier** (post-2012). Recommend either: (a) admit to historical_baseline_2013_2016 tier alongside the existing datacell-v-valitor-iceland-district-court-2012-07 candidate; or (b) admit here as the WikiLeaks-blockade closing endpoint with admission_tier=precursor_endpoint. Either way, the District Court 2012-07 ruling is the in-tier anchor.

candidates.title: EU Council 2012/152/CFSP / SWIFT disconnection of sanctioned Iranian banks (incl. CBI)
candidates.rationale: EU Council Decision 2012/152/CFSP adopted 2012-03-15, effective 2012-03-17 16:00 GMT, prohibited SWIFT from providing messaging services to EU-sanctioned Iranian banks. ~30 banks including the Central Bank of Iran disconnected. **Useful as a non-crypto financial-censorship comparator** — the closest pre-Bitcoin analogue to chain-level OFAC/sanctions cascades in the existing dataset (e.g., infura-metamask-donetsk-luhansk-block-2022-03 mechanism). **Out of scope for direct admission**: this is a sanctions-policy action on the traditional financial system; chain-layer cascade observability is zero. P2 / deferred: useful citation in the dataset's literature-review / discussion sections rather than as an admitted event.

candidates.title: Pecunix transfers gold bullion out of Mat Securitas Express AG (Zurich)
candidates.rationale: Pecunix (founded 2002, Panama, founder Simon Davis) transferred its gold bullion in 2008 from Mat Securitas Express AG (Zurich) to an undisclosed location amid post-e-Gold regulatory pressure on digital-gold-currency providers. No regulator enforcement action, no contemporaneous news pin. The 2008 bullion transfer was an internal corporate move framed by industry observers as a regulatory-arbitrage response. P2 / needs_check: lack of an enforcer-side trigger date and no primary source beyond corporate blog and Wikipedia. Useful only as discussion-section context for the post-e-Gold digital-gold-currency exodus.

candidates.title: SUGEF (Costa Rica) denial of Liberty Reserve money-transmitter license + criminal investigation
candidates.rationale: Costa Rica's Superintendencia General de Entidades Financieras (SUGEF) refused to license Liberty Reserve as a money transmitter in 2011, citing 'lack of transparency about how the business was funded.' Criminal investigation opened 2011-03-07 following 'suspicious bank activity'. Liberty Reserve formally disbanded but continued operating through five shell companies (Budovsky direction). The 2011 Costa Rican regulatory action is the in-tier anchor for the Liberty Reserve trajectory; the 2013-05-28 FinCEN §311 designation and DOJ takedown are out-of-tier (post-2012). Admit as the pre-2013 regulatory predicate. **Coverage caveat**: primary documentary record is dominated by 2013 post-takedown reporting; pin the 2011 Tico Times / La República archive snapshots.

candidates.title: Wau-Holland-Stiftung tax-exempt status challenge by FA Kassel (DE)
candidates.rationale: Finanzamt Kassel (FA Kassel, German tax authority) announced 2010-12-15 that the Wau-Holland-Stiftung's charitable / tax-exempt status would be reviewed and potentially revoked. WHS had collected $1.9M for WikiLeaks Oct 2009-Dec 2010. After ~2 years of negotiations, FA Kassel restored charitable status going forward and retroactively for 2011, but explicitly *not* for 2010 — i.e., a partial tax-status censorship event. Documented by the WHS itself (wauland.de) and Wikipedia. Useful as the only nation-state-tax-authority leg of the WikiLeaks blockade; pairs with the PostFinance and Visa Europe candidates.

candidates.title: Mizuho Bank pressures Mt. Gox to close correspondent account
candidates.rationale: Mizuho Bank (Tokyo branch handling Mt. Gox correspondent) began pressuring Mt. Gox to close its account in late 2012 / early 2013 over rising transaction volumes and US-investigation concerns. Direct upstream of the 2013-06-20 USD-withdrawal suspension (already in corpus as mtgox-usd-withdrawal-suspension-2013-06). **Documented retrospectively** in 2013-2016 reporting (Wired Nov 2013, US class-action litigation 2016+); no contemporaneous 2012 Mizuho statement or Mt. Gox disclosure exists. Useful as the in-tier predicate for mtgox-usd-withdrawal-suspension-2013-06 but only via retrospective forensic reporting. P2 / needs_check.
